summary: Somalia's Immigration and Citizenship Agency says that from 1 September 2025 all foreign nationals wishing to travel to Somalia must apply online for their entry authorisation in advance of their journey, rather than on arrival, through the official portal at etas.gov.so. Its eTAS portal, in an archived copy, says holders of passports from Rwanda and Malaysia are granted visa-free entry, and those from Djibouti, Ethiopia, Burundi, Mauritania, Tanzania, Uganda, Algeria, Libya, Tunisia, Egypt and Comoros are eligible for visas on arrival. The UK government says the eVisa is not considered valid for entry at Hargeisa, where you must buy a single-entry visa on arrival.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says that to enter Somalia, including Somaliland, your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement: WHO's country list gives Somalia's country requirement at entry as no, and the US CDC says the vaccine is not required. Both say vaccination is generally not recommended for travel to the regions of Bakool, Banaadir, Bay, Galguduud, Gedo, Hiiraan, Lower and Middle Juba and Lower and Middle Shabelle, and the CDC says it is not recommended for other areas.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: The US CDC recommends that travellers going to Somalia take prescription medicine to prevent malaria, and to keep taking the rest of the pills after returning home if a doctor prescribed antimalarial medicine.

source.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Travelers' health: Somalia

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for Somalia. The UK government advises adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover the cost of any medical treatment abroad, evacuation by air ambulance and repatriation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Somalia travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward-ticket requirement for Somalia. The US State Department says travellers arriving without an onward ticket and/or clear reason for travel may be refused entry.

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Somalia.

source.name: Immigration and Citizenship Agency of Somalia — Our services: visa services and their requirements (no funds requirement listed)

currencyLimits.text: The UK government says that in Somaliland you must declare cash or travellers cheques if the value is 10,000 US dollars or more. No official source we could read states a threshold for the rest of Somalia.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Somalia travel advice: entry requirements

notes: The UK government says the drinking and sale of alcohol is banned in Somalia.

The UK government says khat is a legal drug in Somalia but it is an offence to take it out of the country, that officials regularly search bags at Hargeisa and Mogadishu airports, and that anyone found in possession of khat is likely to face criminal prosecution.

payments.text: The UK government says credit cards are not widely accepted in Somalia and it is not possible to get currency advances using a credit card, and that the US dollar is the main currency for exchanging. Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and that ATMs are available in major cities, usually in hotels, malls and other secure areas.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil, where it advises against all but essential travel; Canada advises avoiding all travel. The UK says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Somalia, including Somaliland, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping throughout Somalia, including in Somaliland.

tips.text: The UK government advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil, where it advises against all but essential travel; Canada advises avoiding all travel to Somalia. The UK says travelling by road in Somalia is dangerous and that you should get advice from a security firm or a sponsoring organisation.

The UK government says that if you are travelling to Hargeisa International Airport you may be asked to present the Somali eVisa to board your flight, but it will not be considered valid for entry in Hargeisa; you must buy a single-entry visa on arrival there, valid for one month.

The Immigration and Citizenship Agency says that from 1 September 2025 all foreign nationals wishing to travel to Somalia must apply for their entry authorisation online, in advance of their journey. It encourages visitors to apply well ahead of their planned travel dates, to rely only on the official platform at etas.gov.so, and to keep a copy of their approved authorisation for presentation on arrival.

The UK government says credit cards are not widely accepted in Somalia and the US dollar is the main currency for exchanging, and that in Hargeisa you can withdraw US dollars from ATMs using international credit and debit cards.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Somalia?
faq.answer: Somalia's Immigration and Citizenship Agency says that since 1 September 2025 all foreign nationals wishing to travel to Somalia must apply for their entry authorisation online, before departure rather than on arrival, through etas.gov.so. Its eTAS portal, in an archived copy, lists exceptions: Rwanda and Malaysia (visa-free entry) and Djibouti, Ethiopia, Burundi, Mauritania, Tanzania, Uganda, Algeria, Libya, Tunisia, Egypt and Comoros (visas on arrival). No official source we could read publishes the eVisa fee.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Somalia?
faq.answer: No. The UK government advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil, where it advises against all but essential travel, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks; Canada advises avoiding all travel to Somalia. The UK says it can offer only limited consular support.

faq.question: Is Somaliland's visa different from Somalia's?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says that if you are travelling to Hargeisa International Airport you may be asked to present the Somali eVisa to board your flight, but it will not be considered valid for entry in Hargeisa; you must buy a single-entry visa on arrival at Hargeisa International Airport, valid for one month.

faq.question: Can I pay for the Somali visa on arrival in cash?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states a fee. The eTAS portal, in an archived copy, says citizens of countries exempted from eTAS will get a free visa on arrival; for everyone else, the Immigration and Citizenship Agency says that since 1 September 2025 all foreign nationals must apply for their entry authorisation online before travelling.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Somalia?
faq.answer: No. WHO's country list gives Somalia's country requirement at entry as no, and the US CDC says the vaccine is not required for entry.
